scraped.scraped_description: OpenStreetMap users in HOT's priority regions

name: Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team (HOT)
tagline: Mapping for impact in humanitarian crises and development challenges
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
dependency_risks: OpenStreetMap data quality and coverage variability
awards: UN recognition for humanitarian mapping contributions
policy_outcomes: Integration of HOT maps into UN humanitarian response protocols
Adoption by national governments for disaster preparedness planning
Influence on open data policies in development agencies
documented_limitations: Data quality varies by region and volunteer expertise
Coverage gaps in remote or conflict-affected areas
Sustainability of volunteer engagement over time
failure_modes: Incomplete or inaccurate mapping in low-connectivity regions
Political sensitivities around mapping in disputed territories
curation_criteria: OpenStreetMap contribution guidelines, HOT community standards, humanitarian need assessment
contributor_governance: Community-driven with HOT staff oversight; contributors follow OpenStreetMap wiki guidelines and HOT-specific mapping standards
controversies: Debates over mapping accuracy and validation in conflict zones
Questions about whose priorities drive mapping projects
government_partnerships: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
political_relevance_summary: Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team (HOT) addresses making civic data accessible and actionable and enabling broader democratic participation. It has documented policy impact.

movement_building_utility.notes: Serves as an information resource: Mapping for impact in humanitarian crises and development challenges.

generalizability_notes: Open-source codebase enables replication. already deployed internationally across multiple jurisdictions.
